correctness.rationale: On the stated beta-weighted disk L2 complement, exact P+Q insertion in normal ambient multiplication proves K=P M Q M* P-P M* Q M P. Each angular mode of the harmonic Bergman subspace is rank one; consequently every K angular sector is a difference of at most two rank-one operators. Complex conjugation pairs opposite angular sectors and reverses K. For k>=m the first generator is harmonic and vanishes on projection, giving the explicit strictly positive b_k; for 1<=k<m the two projected radial powers are linearly independent, giving determinant -[A_k B_k-G_k^2]<0 and the two eigenvalue roots. k=0 cancels. The gamma moment quotient has the verified k^-2 tail coefficient m²(alpha+1); trace norm is obtained from a finite central sum and exact telescoping. A separate stdlib checker passed 177256 exact finite-mode assertions, including the m=2 alpha=0 norm overshoot; finite checks supplement rather than prove the infinite theorem. Domain, signs, spectral multiplicities and boundary alpha>-1/m>=1 are explicit.

originality.rationale: The verified new statement is the complete signed eigenvalue multiset for dual Toeplitz multiplication by a single monomial on the beta-weighted harmonic Bergman complement, with explicit central 2x2 Gram eigenvalues and nuclear norm. Wang–Zhao (2021) prove qualitative hyponormal-normal equivalence and monomial normality, not spectral eigenvalues. The two closest published spectral findings act on different operator spaces (harmonic subspace versus its complement; analytic complement versus harmonic complement). An example at m=1 alpha=0 gives different norms 1/6 and 1/12 for harmonic and dual harmonic compressions, ruling out a literal reuse of their formulas. Extensive actual claim-focused and structural searches returned no dominating result. An inaccessible Peng–Zhao (2021) paper remains a non-decisive priority risk: published abstract describes the spectrum of S rather than the self-commutator K, but full text might contain additional facts.

value.rationale: This natural complement compression is not a minor substitution of the harmonic-subspace operator: it has infinite-dimensional radial sectors with genuinely nontrivial two-vector central Gram interactions. The theorem supplies the entire spectrum and multiplicity, sharp signed counting constants, the trace norm as a finite formula for every beta weight and degree, and a concrete exact operator-norm overshoot by the central sector. These invariants quantify the obstruction to normality beyond the known qualitative theorem and are useful for comparing Toeplitz compressions and operator ideal behavior.
